corrections.finding: Dropped measures (amplitude ratio 1:3.3, leg weighting factors 1.2/0.6/0.4/0.4, the 0.1 reduction, the halving) and dropped 'always'; 'quieting' is vaguer than a 0.1 reduction of the posterior legs' factor.
corrections.fixed_text: A wandering spider on a vibrating platform is always turning toward the legs a vibration reaches first, onsets 4 ms apart, or toward the legs it reaches with larger amplitude, amplitudes in the ratio 1 to 3.3; its four legs' weighting factors are 1.2, 0.6, 0.4, 0.4; a vibration reaching a front leg is lowering the factor of the legs behind it on its own side by 0.1, and with vibration reaching both sides this lowering is going front to back alone and is halving the factor; its turning is less exact as the source is further behind it.

corrections.finding: Dead word 'third' in 'two to the third'; and 'by no magnitude' plus 'still-possibling' contradict item 1, where larger amplitude also decides the spider's direction.
corrections.fixed_text: Eight legs are three binaries, left or right across, front or back along, and first or not first in sequence, two times two times two being eight: each leg is opening with its prior and the parity it is observing, a leg and its partner across are agreeing or parting now, and the spider's turning is its next, five dimensions resolving in two directions, a vibration coming inward along the legs and the spider's turning going outward, its direction resolving by the sequence of its legs' changing or by the larger amplitude on its legs.

corrections.finding: Source says stilts overestimate and stumps underestimate travel distance and the odometer integrates strides; 'overshooting its home' and 'stopping short' go past that, and the odometer integrating strides is replaced by 'a sequence of strides'.
corrections.fixed_text: A desert ant walking out and homing is going by its strides, an odometer adding them up: with stilts on its legs it is overestimating the distance it travels, with stumps for legs it is underestimating it, its stride rate and speed barely changing.

corrections.finding: Claim stronger: source has minimal background pattern motion causing about a centimetre drift, time to adapt not eliminating it; text drops 'minimal', adds 'at a feeder' and 'with it' (direction), and 'leaving in place' overstates 'did not eliminate'; 'within millimetres' loosens 'to the millimetre'.
corrections.fixed_text: A hovering hummingbird is holding its place to the millimetre by steadying the visual motion about it; when a background pattern is moving even minimally, it is drifting about a centimetre, and time to adapt is not removing the drifting.

corrections.finding: Claim stronger: source says halteres signal the counter-turn, not that it ends each turn; 'ahead' on the expanding image is not in the source.
corrections.fixed_text: A fruit fly is exploring by straight flights and sudden turns, each turn about 90 degrees in under 50 ms, all or none, left or right; an expanding image is triggering a turn, an attractive odour is changing how often and where turns come, and its halteres, its balance organs, are signalling the counter-turn.

corrections.finding: Measure changed: 'many' of its turns for 'most'; 'ahead of the image's drifting' loses the near-perfect synchrony with the motions that would cause drift (compensating before drift); body follows head-body angles; 'from its perch' not in source; internal models are the authors' conclusion, not 'a field's'.
corrections.fixed_text: A hunting dragonfly is catching its prey about 95 times in 100, pursuing and snatching in under half a second, its head turning in near-perfect synchrony with the motions that would make the prey's image drift, so compensating before any drift, and its body turning in following its head-body angles, most of its turns coming with no change in the prey's motion; the authors' explaining of internal models stands apart from this observing.

corrections.finding: Dissolved word 'thirds' (two thirds); 'each arm with thousands of suckers' is stronger than the source (thousands of suckers on the animal); taste cells fire continuously but only during direct contact, and 'only' is dropped; 'partly' loosens 'semi-independently'.
corrections.fixed_text: An octopus has two out of three of its neurons in its eight arms, and thousands of suckers moving on their own; a sucker's taste cells are signalling continuously but only during direct contact, its touch cells only at a touching's opening, and an arm is tasting semi-independently.
